---
title: subdifferential of absolute value at zero
tags: [mathematics]
---

## Prompt

Find $\partial f(0)$ for $f(x)=|x|$, and prove both necessity and sufficiency.

## Statement

For $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, $f(x)=|x|$,

$$
\partial f(0)=[-1,1].
$$

Every number in this interval is a supporting slope at zero.

## Proof

The defining inequality at zero is $|z|\geq gz$ for every $z\in\mathbb R$.
For $z>0$, division by $z$ gives $g\leq1$.
For $z<0$, division reverses the inequality and gives $g\geq-1$.
These conditions are necessary.

Conversely, if $g\in[-1,1]$, then for $z\geq0$, $gz\leq z=|z|$; for $z<0$, $gz\leq-z=|z|$.
The inequality holds everywhere, so these conditions are also sufficient.
